body: `require "bundler/setup"` in a library file can have surprising side effects (activates Bundler, changes load paths) and can also raise `LoadError` in environments that use RubyGems directly. Prefer requiring bundler only in executables/CLI entrypoints, or guard this require so `Udb::Paths` remains usable without Bundler.

In `f32_div`, the significands are compared using `$signed(sigA) < $signed(sigB)`. These are unsigned magnitudes (and may have bit 31 set after shifting), so a signed compare will produce incorrect normalization decisions. Use an unsigned comparison (`sigA < sigB`) or explicitly cast to unsigned.

In `softfloat_roundToUI64`, `sig = sig & ~64'1;` uses a nonstandard literal form (`64'1`). This likely won’t parse and should be `~64'h1` (or equivalent) to clear the LSB for the tie-to-even case.
```suggestion
        sig = sig & ~64'h1;
```

`packToF32UI` now takes a 32-bit `sig` and packs using arithmetic addition. If `sig` contains bit 23 (implicit leading 1) or any higher bits, it will carry into the exponent/sign fields and corrupt the result (e.g., `i64_to_f32` passes `absA << shiftDist`, which will typically include the implicit bit). `packToF32UI` should only pack the 23-bit fraction (mask/`sig[22:0]`) or keep the prior concatenation-style packing with a `Bits<23>` argument.
```suggestion
    return (sign `<< 31) + (exp `<< 23) + (sig & 0x7FFFFF);
```

In `softfloat_roundToI64`, both overflow returns use `I64_NEG_OVERFLOW` regardless of sign. For positive overflow this should return `I64_POS_OVERFLOW` (and similarly in the later overflow check), otherwise positive overflow saturates to the wrong value.

In `fmax.s`, the both-NaN case hardcodes `32'h7fc00000` instead of using `SP_CANONICAL_NAN` (used elsewhere). Using the constant avoids divergence if the canonical NaN definition changes and keeps `fmin.s`/`fmax.s` consistent.
```suggestion
      f[fd] = SP_CANONICAL_NAN; # canonical NaN
```

This is intentional softfloat behavior. `packToF32UI` uses `+` rather than `|` so that a 24-bit significand (bit 23 set) naturally carries into the exponent field — this is how rounding up `1.111...1` to `10.0` increments the exponent without a separate branch. `softfloat_roundPackToF32` produces a sig with at most bit 24 set (after `(sig + roundIncrement) >> 7`), and that carry is deliberate. The direct call sites either pass sig=0, a value known to be ≤23 bits, or a value shifted to place the leading 1 at bit 23 (which may carry into bit 24 on rounding). Masking to `sig & 0x7FFFFF` would break the rounding path.

False positive — dist==0 is never reachable at any call site. Every caller either passes a constant nonzero distance, guards with `> 0` before calling, or is in a branch where the sign of the computed value guarantees nonzero. The description already documents the precondition ("dist must not be zero"), which is always satisfied.

False positive — dist==0 is never reachable at any call site. Tracing through `f32_muladd`: line 536 passes `32 - expDiff` (reached only when `expDiff <= 0`, so dist >= 32); line 539 passes `expDiff` (reached only when `expDiff > 0`); line 553 passes `-expDiff` (reached only when `expDiff < 0`); line 566 passes `expDiff` (reached only when `expDiff > 0`); line 572 passes `-shiftDist` where the branch condition `$signed(shiftDist) < 0s` ensures shiftDist != 0. All other call sites are guarded by `shiftDist > 0` or pass a constant. The description already documents the precondition ("dist must not be zero"), which is always satisfied.
